abstract: Majorana zero modes (MZMs) are promising for topological quantum computation, with vortices in topological superconductors serving as a leading platform. Recent experiments show that integer Abrikosov vortices in iron-based superconductors can split into fractional vortices (FVs) carrying fractional flux quanta. We show that due to topological protection, MZMs hosted by FVs are spatially unfolded over the FV cores, while fermionic bound states remain localized at individual FV cores. This yields zero-bias conductance peaks in both local tunneling and nonlocal crossed Andreev reflection, offering an alternative MZM signature.

title: Selective effects of selenium substitution on superconductivity and magnetic memory in 4Hb-TaS2
abstract: Disorder plays a central role in correlated quantum materials, but its effects can be highly selective when several electronic orders coexist. The van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2 provides such a case, combining superconductivity, charge-order tendencies, strong scattering, and magnetic memory manifested through spontaneous vortices. Here we use Se substitution as a controlled local perturbation of the disorder landscape in 4Hb-TaS2. We find that superconductivity remains remarkably robust while the magnetic memory is strongly suppressed at higher Se concentrations. These results show that Se substitution does not create the hidden magnetic memory, but instead selectively weakens its macroscopic manifestation. More broadly, they reveal a sharp separation between robust superconducting and hidden-memory phases, and a highly disorder-sensitive spontaneous-vortex response in 4Hb-TaS2.

title: Evidence for an effective gauge field in flakes of superconducting 4Hb-TaS2
abstract: Understanding the normal state of unconventional superconductors is central to uncovering the origin of superconductivity itself. Unconventional superconductivity often emerges from correlated electronic states characterized by intertwined symmetry-breaking orders. A striking example is 4Hb-TaS2, whose superconducting state exhibits a remarkable range of phenomena, including an unusual magnetic memory effect. Previous experiments showed that magnetic memory can be encoded above Tc and later revealed through spontaneous vortices below Tc, suggesting time-reversal symmetry breaking. However, since memory and vorticity are intertwined, this prevents establishing whether the effect results from trapped flux, weak conventional magnetism, or a true hidden electronic order. Here, we show that magnetic memory persists in the vortex-free Meissner regime of exfoliated 4Hb-TaS2 flakes, where it appears as a stable remanent modification of the superconducting screening response. Our results rule out explanations based on trapped vortices. Furthermore, the spatial profile of the flux generated by trained samples at zero field is inconsistent with conventional weak magnetism, suggesting a hidden electronic phase that imprints an effective flux on the superconducting condensate.

title: Chiral superconductivity on a closed Klein bottle: a chirality wall and its Majorana seam spectrum
abstract: We study a spinless $\pi$-flux lattice superconductor whose normal-state momentum-space fundamental domain is a Klein bottle. Within this model, a glide lift and a hidden antiunitary symmetry independently force the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) Chern number to vanish. A diagonal pairing breaks the antiunitary obstruction exactly when its real part is nonzero; this is necessary, not sufficient, for a chiral phase. We derive explicit Pfaffians determining Chern parity and identify three analytic families of gap closings in a real-pairing section. For a chiral state on a closed real-space Klein bottle, the prescribed pairing and gluing produce a $\Delta C=2$ chirality wall. A translation-invariant unfolding resolves two co-propagating Majorana branches. Their finite-size levels depend on circumference and holonomy; the near-zero pair is lifted at first order by allowed local seam perturbations. A cut-cylinder control has the same low-energy channel count, so gluing reconnects existing gapless content. We also distinguish literal gluing from deck projection: particle--hole symmetry exchanges the deck eigenblocks, precluding their interpretation as independent BdG quotient Hamiltonians. The contribution is a model-specific account of pairing compatibility and closed-surface seam spectra. The energy cost is evaluated for a fixed pairing background; neither a protected zero mode nor a self-consistent wall solution is claimed.

title: Chiral $p$-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moir\'e Chern Band
abstract:
We study a spin-polarized moir'e Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ with short-range repulsion, finding superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator at filling $
u=2/3$ and a topological charge density wave at $
u=3/4$. Exact diagonalization reveals pair binding over $0.7\lesssim
u\lesssim0.77$, consistent with experiment, along with finite superfluid stiffness, chiral $p$-wave pairing correlations, and adiabatic connectivity to an attractive model. At weak repulsion, Kohn-Luttinger theory supports a Fermi-surface instability with the same pairing symmetry. The superconducting state has a Bogoliubov-de Gennes Chern number $C_{\mathrm{BdG}}=-1$, opposite to the normal-state Chern number at $
u=1$. Our results reveal interplay among superconductivity, fractional topology, and charge order.

title: Tan's Contact for Trapped Spin-Orbit-Coupled Fermi Gases at Finite Temperature
abstract: Tan's contact, bridging microscopic features of many-body quantum systems to two-body contact interactions, is pivotal in the description of quantum gases. However, past studies of Tan's contact of the spin-orbit coupled Fermi gases have been exclusively discussed at zero temperature. The thermal effects on that, which cannot be neglected in most experimental conditions, has not been explored so far. Here, through a path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) study, we show that thermal effects fundamentally alter the scaling relation between spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Tan's contact. The linear scaling of Tan's contact with respect to the strength of SOC found at zero temperature is drastically undermined by the thermal effects. And a new mechanism based on the competition between the mean occupancy and the energy-reweighted occupancy of the opposite spin fermion pairs within the interaction range has been unveiled, which radically changes the above linear scaling to a non-monotonic dependence. Our work should be useful for future experiments to explore the preternatural thermal effects on Tan's contact of the strongly interacting spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas.

title: Nonreciprocal Floquet tunneling dynamics of spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a non-Hermitian double-well potential
abstract: The stable tunneling dynamics in non-Hermitian quantum systems is one of the fundamental issues in the study of quantum transport. Nonreciprocal coupling, as another crucial manifestation of non-Hermiticity, exerts significant regulatory effects on the stability of quantum devices and on spin tunneling dynamics. Here we place spin-orbit-coupled bosonic atoms in a double-well potential with gain and loss, and investigate the effect of nonreciprocal coupling on the system dynamics. Through an analytical analysis of the Floquet states and the quasi-energy spectrum under periodic driving, we obtain the PT-symmetry phase diagram of the system. We further explore the synergistic regulation mechanism of several factors---including the strength of nonreciprocal coupling, the non-Hermitian strength arising from gain-loss, and the periodic driving---on stable spin-flip tunneling. The results show that precise manipulation of nonreciprocity and gain-loss can substantially enlarge the stable parameter region. In nonreciprocal systems with balanced gain and loss, the continuity or discreteness of the stable parameter region is determined by the parity of the driving-frequency ratio $\Omega/\omega$, and the spin-flip tunneling can be precisely controlled through the parameters $\lambda$ and $2\varepsilon/\omega$. For the unbalanced gain-loss scenario, the equilibrium conditions for achieving stable spin-flip tunneling under different parities of $\Omega/\omega$ are further provided. These findings offer a new theoretical approach for realizing robust spin-flip tunneling, provide guiding significance for the study of quantum-state transport in non-Hermitian ultracold atomic systems, and also serve as a reference for the experimental design of novel spin-based quantum devices.

title: Transverse momentum transport and collective-mode localization in dipolar tube arrays
abstract: We study transverse transport of longitudinal momentum in an array of one-dimensional Bose gases coupled by dipolar interactions without particle tunneling. Within zero-temperature Bogoliubov theory, we characterize this transport using the inter-tube momentum correlator and its squared magnitude, termed amplitude and intensity. In a uniform array, pairs of Bogoliubov quasiparticles propagate ballistically across the tubes, while their dephasing produces a $t^{-3}$ decay of the long-wavelength amplitude. Tube-to-tube density imbalance acts as quenched disorder and localizes the transverse collective modes. At fixed longitudinal momentum, this arrests the growth of the intensity profile, whose time-averaged spatial decay measures the localization length. Equal-time correlations are much less sensitive to disorder and primarily reflect the interaction range: in the uniform array they decay with tube separation as $r^{-7}$ for dipolar coupling, compared with exponential decay for nearest-neighbor coupling. Finally, sufficiently strong inter-tube repulsion destabilizes the longitudinally uniform state toward density modulations staggered between neighboring tubes, at a threshold independent of density imbalance.

title: Metastability, collective excitations, and traveling states of one-dimensional spin-orbit-coupled quantum droplets
abstract: We study the static and traveling droplet phases of spin-orbit coupled, one-dimensional Bose-Bose mixtures with a Lee-Huang-Yang correction. For the static droplets, employing a variational analysis for an infinitely extended mixture, we show that the system can feature two ground-state droplet phases: a stripe droplet phase up to a critical Rabi coupling strength, at which it undergoes a first-order transition to a zero-momentum droplet phase. The variational results for the ground-state properties are shown to be in good agreement with numerical solutions for droplets in the thermodynamic limit as well as finite-size droplets in the "flat-top regime". For finite-size droplets, the stripe phase can feature multiple stationary states with different numbers of peaks in their stripe density patterns. The calculation of the excitation spectrum for these stationary states confirms their stability. To study the moving droplets, we investigate the ground-state phases of the system in the droplet's comoving frame. We show that in the comoving frame, droplets acquire a finite longitudinal magnetization. As a consequence, the phase diagram features two distinct phases: a traveling stripe droplet and a plane-wave droplet. The real-time evolution of these droplets in the space-fixed frame, complemented by the Bogoliubov analysis in the comoving frame, illustrates the stability of these traveling droplet phases.

title: Kelvin-Wave Multiplication by Sound Emission
abstract: A subsonic Kelvin quantum can emit a phonon and split into two softer quanta, increasing Kelvin population while losing energy. In the soft-phonon limit, rotational invariance relates the leading acoustic shear amplitude, odd under reversal of phonon axial momentum, to the energy released. Microscopic calculations support this dispersion dependence. In a reflecting cavity with coherent sound and Kelvin seeds, Gross--Pitaevskii evolution shows Kelvin gain, larger mean-square displacement and smaller mean-square slope; a $\pi$ shift of the initial sound phase reverses these changes.

title: Single-atom billiards in an ultracold bath with energy-tunable collisions and threshold-sensitive detection
abstract: Transport processes at the microscopic scale can differ strongly from their macroscopic counterparts, particularly when the environment is not a well-defined surface but an unordered thermal medium. Ultracold quantum gases offer a high degree of controllability and directly observable dynamics, thereby providing a versatile platform to study such transport processes under precisely controllable conditions. Here, we realize an energy-tunable single-atom collider by transporting individual cesium atoms at controlled velocity through an ultracold rubidium bath. The constant lattice velocity sets the directed contribution to the collision-energy distribution, while the lattice depth provides a tunable energy threshold for collision-induced transport disruption. By independently varying these parameters together with bath density and temperature, we separate the number of collision events from their probability to disrupt transport. Across a regime with only a few expected collisions per passage, the inferred single-collision ejection probability rises from small values to near unity as the collision energy exceeds the lattice confinement scale. The experiment thus converts microscopic collisional energy transfer into a binary single-atom observable and provides a controlled link between individual scattering events and emergent dissipative transport.

title: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system
abstract: The collapse and revival of localized states in many-body systems is a quintessential example of a quantum interference phenomenon that cannot be explained purely within mean-field theories. Historically, the majority of previous work on quantum revivals has been in a Schr\"odinger mechanics context, typically for effectively 1D systems with a focus on the autocorrelation function as the key detection observable. The general revival subject acquires a far greater complexity in the bosonic many-body context that offers a larger variety of observables and intrinsically implies high dimensionality. Here, the focus is on the simplest nontrivial (i.e., not 1D) bosonic many-body system, namely a symmetric two-site Bose-Hubbard model. The non-equilibrium situation of a coherent initial state prepared on one of the two sites of this integrable 2D system in the strongly self-trapping regime is considered. The revival behaviors emerging from the resulting dynamics within expectation values, coherences, and the autocorrelation function are theoretically derived, and the entanglement behavior is illustrated. Several new features, unknown so far in the Schr\"odinger context and identified here in terms of five ``puzzles'', are encountered and discussed, among them, a synchronized resurgence behavior, differing revivals times depending on the specific observable, and a manifestation of a precession that appears in the underlying mean field dynamics. These new phenomena can be entirely understood through a comprehensive semiclassical theory, building upon the underlying classical (mean-field) phase-space structure. A quantitative comparison of the latter with semiclassical predictions and quantum perturbative calculations yields an overall excellent agreement and confirms that a full semiclassical theory is pivotal for the understanding of these genuinely quantum many-body interference phenomena.

title: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas
abstract: We consider a static dipolar impurity immersed in a Fermi gas and show how dipolar interactions shape both the few-body scattering properties and the resulting polaron physics. Using Fumi's theorem, we connect the anisotropic phase shifts directly to the ground-state energy, and compute the exact impurity spectrum via the functional determinant approach. The resulting spectrum is a convolution of independent even- and odd-wave contributions, giving rise to a ground state with simultaneously occupied even- and odd-wave bound states whose separation is tunable via the dipole length. A variational ansatz limited to one particle-hole excitation fails to capture this doubly occupied ground state. We further find that long-range dipolar interactions weaken Anderson's orthogonality catastrophe, reducing the power-law decay of the quasiparticle weight. These effects can be tested with ultracold polar molecules, where microwave shielding and independent tunability of interactions enable experimental access to the predicted regimes.

title: Competition and cancellation in a tilted Rice--Mele chain: exact Wannier--Stark offset and spectral readout
abstract: In a tilted Rice--Mele chain, the Wannier--Stark (WS) ladder becomes staggered, \(E_n=n\Fo+(-1)^{n+1}A\). The offset \(A\) reflects the competition between the staggered onsite energy \(\Delta\) and the dimerized hopping \(\dt\), and its cancellation restores spectral equidistance. We determine \(A\) through a systematic strong-field series in the WS basis and a nonperturbative two-band Floquet expression. An exact matrix element reduces the strong-field expansion to Bessel algebra; at the representative working point, truncation at seventh order locates the cancellation point with a theory-internal truncation error of \(0.010\)~Hz, against \(27.3\)~Hz at first order. The Floquet propagator gives the closed form \(A=(\Fo/\pi)\arcsin(-i\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U/2)\), exact within the two-band model, implying the kinematic bound \(|A|\le\Fo/2\) and identifying cancellation with maximum spectral uniformity. The same analytic structure yields a family of real zeros and complex exceptional points that set the convergence radius of the strong-field series without touching the real axis. On odd-length chains, the hidden-symmetry defect produces a pairing plateau of height \(2|A|\) that persists numerically beyond first order in the modulations, allowing the offset to be read from the static spectrum without Floquet propagation or time evolution. In the bulk, cancellation appears as the merging of two sidebands into a single line at \(\Fo\), a null measurement that requires no calibrated sideband amplitudes, although the tilt and line frequency still need calibration. These signatures provide complementary spectral tests of the staggered WS ladder and a calibration-aware route to precision force sensing.

title: Inferring the Number of Quantum State Transfers with Neural Networks
abstract: Repeated-use quantum state transfer (QST) goes beyond the single-use paradigm by accounting for the memory that accumulates inside the transmission channel when it is not reset between uses. Consequently, the map governing the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ use of the channel differs from use to use and carries a signature of each previous use. We ask whether this use number can be recovered from transmission data alone, and show that it can: a simple feed-forward neural network, given as input the Bloch vectors sent and received over a single use of an XX spin-chain channel, is able to identify the use number with an accuracy exceeding 90%. Exploiting the U(1) symmetry of the channel, we find that a reduced two-component representation of the transmitted states improves the accuracy further, to about 95%. We characterise the dependence of the classifier on the size and composition of the training data, finding that the number of sampled states and of sampled timings are equally important. We also identify the data set sizes required to reach a given accuracy. Finally, we quantify the severity of the residual misclassifications with an earth-mover distance on the confusion matrix.

title: Provably efficient experimental classification of quantum data with quantum kernels
abstract: Analyzing quantum systems is essential for quantum information processing, but can require exponentially many measurements without exploiting the structure of the system or task. Quantum machine learning offers a promising way to reduce this cost by learning from quantum data. Here, we theoretically establish a framework for efficient quantum-state classification and experimentally demonstrate the resulting scheme on a programmable photonic processor. Our analysis links learning efficiency to the structure of quantum data, without relying on a physical description tailored to each task. We derive sufficient conditions for accurate classification with a number of measurements polynomial in system size. We apply this guarantee to a resource problem in continuous-variable (CV) quantum computing: classifying stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity. Experimentally, we implement the classification of single-mode CV quantum states with stellar rank zero and one. This is enabled by developing a programmable CV photonic processor capable of preparing and processing diverse Gaussian and non-Gaussian states and performing virtual projection onto such states, going beyond the Gaussian-only capabilities of most existing photonic platforms. The experiment demonstrates accurate classification despite experimental imperfections. Our results establish a theory-guided and experimentally validated framework for quantum-state classification that can be implemented on quantum devices available today.

title: Conditional Information Flow and Neural Representability of One-Dimensional Rotated Cluster States
abstract: I study how measurement outcomes can remain conditionally dependent over long distances while the underlying state carries only a small internal memory, using one-dimensional rotated cluster states, whose exact matrix product state (MPS) bond dimension is $D=2$ at every rotation angle. Using exact MPS contraction, I compute the conditional mutual information (CMI) of two readout protocols: the entanglement-swapping endpoint CMI decreases from one bit at $\theta=0$ to zero at $\theta=\pi/2$, whereas a stationary bulk readout of the locally equivalent conventional cluster state vanishes at both limits. As an exact control, the spin-1 AKLT chain obeys $I_m=(4/9)\,3^{-m}$, so its CMI length equals its two-point correlation length, for an identifiable but non-generic reason. I then compare learners on the same $N=64$, $\theta=0.35$ target. A positive autoregressive GRU learns the computational-basis Born distribution from a few thousand samples, but an exactly computable Bell-basis readout shows that this distribution does not fix the phases. A complex RBM reaches the $N=8$ ground state under an exact objective, while a short generic recurrent variational Monte Carlo pilot is still improving when its runs end. As a positive control, an MPS-induced recurrent model whose hidden state is the bond vector reaches the ground state to near machine precision at $\chi=2$, whereas a $\chi=1$ control fails. These results show that long CMI does not require a large bond dimension, and that building the small virtual memory into the architecture greatly eases optimization.

title: Digital-Analog Quantum Neural Network with Long-Range Interactions
abstract: Protocols combining single-qubit digital operations with analog quantum evolutions bypass large numbers of two-qubit entangling gates, offering a promising approach to variational algorithms and hybrid quantum simulation. Focusing on the digital-analog quantum neural network (DA-QNN) as a representative framework, this work demonstrates that incorporating long-range interactions enhances the efficiency of such hybrid algorithms. Within the analog blocks, an Ising model with power-law interactions is employed to generate entanglement, and this protocol is benchmarked across supervised and unsupervised learning tasks. Beyond discussing the effects of the transverse field and evolution time, the primary analysis focuses on how the interaction range governs the expressibility and trainability of the ansatz. For supervised image classification and many-body phase detection, long-range ansatzes match the performance of their short-range counterparts with fewer DA-QNN layers or shorter evolution times, owing to the rapid information propagation across the system enabled by nonlocal couplings. This resource reduction alleviates the classical optimization overhead and eases experimental implementation. In unsupervised phase detection, although the long-range ansatz does not outperform its short-range counterpart in every regime, the two ansatzes provide complementary signatures that jointly reconstruct the complete phase diagram. These findings establish long-range interacting platforms as a compelling resource for advancing practical, large-scale digital-analog quantum computing.

title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding for Nuclear Deformation Landscapes
abstract: Locating the minimum of a nuclear collective landscape can require many interacting many-body calculations. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family with a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle. The oracle supplies the predicate required for quantum minimum-finding without first constructing the energy landscape point by point. We implement it for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model using circuit-generated energy estimates during the search. In a four-point calculation, one Grover round raises the probability of the true minimum from 0.25 to 0.921. A $4\times4$ quadrupole--octupole-field calculation extends the complete circuit to two coordinates, although its minimum is first sampled in a round with zero Grover iterations. Its worst-case branch-preparation fidelity of 0.744 falls below the declared target, identifying coherent ground-state access as the current bottleneck. QDMin inherits expected $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ candidate-query scaling in the unstructured model; total advantage depends on the many-body oracle cost and remains unestablished.

title: Fast and accurate neural triage decoding of ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes
abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing. High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have emerged as a promising approach to reducing the substantial physical qubit overhead of quantum error correction, enabling encoding rates exceeding $1/2$ in blocks of approximately one thousand physical data qubits. However, their practical implementation requires decoders that combine high accuracy with low latency to keep pace with quantum hardware. Existing decoders of high-rate qLDPC codes can achieve high accuracy but often incur substantial computational latency, whereas neural network decoders have yet to be demonstrated for high-rate qLDPC codes. Here, we introduce \emph{neural triage decoding}, a framework that uses syndrome consistency to adaptively allocate neural computation. A local neural message-passing network rapidly predicts error corrections, additional iterations reduce residual syndrome violations, and a rarely invoked diversification stage searches for consistent corrections to the remaining shots. We demonstrate that the \texttt{Triage} decoder can decode ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes encoding a few hundred logical qubits, including lifted-product and Kasai codes, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy comparable to the near optimal algorithmic decoders while reducing decoding latency by approximately one to two orders of magnitude. Our framework is inspired by a rigorous analysis of the exact bitwise marginal decoder, revealing a distance-independent syndrome-inconsistent error floor. In addition, we show the robustness of neural network decoders to mismatched error priors. Our results establish adaptive neural decoding as a promising route towards fast, accurate, and scalable quantum error correction in the near term.

title: Probing fluctuations in photon emission statistics of spin injected quantum dots with time dependent electronic excitation
abstract: Electrically spin-injected ensembles of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots emit circularly polarized single photons, with the emission helicity determined by the spin polarization of the injected electrons. A ferromagnetic CoFeB spin-injection layer with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, combined with an MgO tunnel barrier, enables spin-polarized electron injection into the quantum-dot active region, resulting in circularly polarized photon emission at zero applied magnetic field. These devices realize direct spin-charge-photon conversion in an electrically driven, microelectronics-compatible quantum light source that operates without an external pump laser. Using an extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer with four detectors and time-tagged readout, we measure time-resolved photon-number statistics that resolve up to $|2\rangle$ Fock states within a single excitation cycle. While single-photon ($n=|1\rangle$) emission tracks the electrical excitation pulse as expected, the two-photon ($n=|2\rangle$) statistics exhibit pronounced fluctuations at multiple temporal positions within the pulse. These fluctuations vanish upon demagnetization of the spin-injection layer, establishing a direct link between the multi-photon emission dynamics and the spin polarization of the injected carriers. The observations indicate that spin injection controls not only the helicity of the emitted photons but also higher-order temporal correlations of the emission. The behavior is phenomenologically captured by inserting both a variable excitation mechanism and a set of multi-emitter collapse operators within a stochastic wave function evolution. The platform thus opens a route to electrically driven, spin-controlled single and multi-photon Fock-state sources and provides a testbed for spin-conditioned multi-emitter dynamics in solid-state quantum light sources.

title: Where the Error Lives: Spectral Representations of Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians
abstract: Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) is the standard method for computing the electronic structure of molecules and materials, but its self-consistent-field (SCF) iterations make it expensive for large systems and high-throughput screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonian models offer a shortcut: an equivariant network predicts the Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian matrix in one forward pass, and diagonalizing the prediction yields orbital energies, the HOMO-LUMO gap, molecular orbitals and the electron density. These models are trained to match the reference matrix entry by entry, yet a small entry-wise error does not guarantee accurate eigenvalues or eigenvectors. Two physics-informed alternatives go partway: a recently proposed wavefunction-alignment loss adds a spectral penalty without diagonalizing the prediction, and matching the electron density of the diagonalized prediction supervises it directly. Neither is complete: by representing the prediction error in the eigenbasis of the reference Hamiltonian, we show that each sees only part of the error, and that shifting the predicted orbital energies leaves the electron density exactly unchanged. The same analysis identifies a complete training signal: the cumulative local density of states (cumulative LDOS), the number of electrons at each point in space with energy below a given threshold. The cumulative LDOS is a single physical observable that contains the electron density as a special case, responds to every component of the error, determines the Hamiltonian uniquely, and yields gradients that do not vanish for large orbitalenergy errors. Fine-tuning three Hamiltonian networks on QH9 in this way, which we call FermiScope, reduces the HOMO-LUMO gap error without increasing the element-wise error. The gains carry over to out-of-distribution and molecular-dynamics splits, where the wavefunction-alignment loss helps less.

title: Uncertainty-Driven Self-Refinement of Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Fitting Nonadiabatic Potential Energy Surface
abstract: In this work, we propose an uncertainty-driven self-refinement learning method using adaptive Chebyshev-polynomial-based Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (ChebyKANs) to build potential energy surface (PES). Unlike conventional approaches, our method employs a main-model-plus-residual-model architecture for automatic sampling based on a hybrid criterion, where sampling and fitting are decoupled. To benchmark our method, the non-adiabatic two-state PES of the H + H$_2$ system is constructed using a database computed at the multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) level with a rather large active space. Our calculations show that the proposed architectural design makes the efficiency gain, and that KAN offers enhanced interpretability over conventional neural network (NN) fitting methods through its mathematically well-understood basis functions. Furthermore, the present calculations accurately reproduce all important conformations on the PES, including the transition state and the conical intersection. Then, the multi-configurational time-dependent Hartree (MCTDH) method reproduces the non-adiabatic dynamics with results in close agreement with previously reported findings.

title: Hydration Free Energies from Local Electronic Structures
abstract: Free energies of solvation are crucial to our understanding of chemical reactions, particularly when these take place in water. However, computing changes in free energies associated with the process of immersing arbitrary molecules in an aqueous solution both accurately and efficiently with the use of one universal method remains challenging. By means of atomic decompositions of total (bulk) energies from Kohn-Sham density functional theory in a basis of spatially localized molecular orbitals, the present study enables the computation of hydration free energies from local electronic-structure objects derived in the condensed phase. Specifically, our protocol computes an enthalpy of hydration as the sum of the decomposed change in internal energy of a solute upon solvation and a newly developed term that accounts for the response of the environment, which may then be combined with a standard expression for the corresponding change in entropy. In applications to eight neutral solutes in water, internal energies are all found to converge rapidly and in a smooth manner upon an increase in the size of the solvated cluster, and the corresponding enthalpies and free energies of hydration are likewise found to agree with experimental references within statistical uncertainty.

title: PolyDiscover: an integrated trust-aware platform for multi-objective polymer discovery and simulation validation
abstract: Data-driven polymer discovery remains fragmented across databases, models, screening, literature, and simulations. We present PolyDiscover, a platform unifying multi-source property lookup, graph-neural-network prediction, trust-aware multi-objective screening, literature extraction, generative candidate exploration, and automated handoff to molecular-dynamics validation. Building on published ADEPT-PolyGraphMT, it harmonizes experimental, molecular-dynamics, density-functional-theory, and group-contribution data spanning 28 properties across about 13,000 real and one million virtual polymers. Its engine combines feasibility filtering and exact Pareto ranking with a trust score integrating similarity to known polymers, physical consistency, predictive uncertainty, and synthesizability, followed by diversity-aware shortlisting. Two case studies on lightweight, thermally stable structural materials and thermally stable electrical insulators, using monomer HOMO-LUMO gap as an insulation proxy, reduced a million-polymer search space to 30 chemically diverse candidates per task. Higher-fidelity molecular-dynamics and density-functional-theory calculations, interpreted after correcting systematic density underestimation by the molecular-dynamics protocol, showed retention of targeted property combinations. Ablation showed that trust-aware ranking shifted about one fifth of each shortlist toward more synthesizable chemistry closer to known polymers. A constrained natural-language interface translated a free-text request into a validated specification matching expert screening exactly, while staged literature evidence corroborated high glass-transition temperatures in polyimide-dominated shortlists against published experiments. PolyDiscover offers a traceable route from design intent to simulation-validated candidates, easing exploration of polymer chemical space.

title: Distilling Large-Scale Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials to Predict Long-Timescale Electrolyte Transport Properties
abstract: Accurately predicting the transport properties of liquid electrolytes is critical for next-generation battery design and requires force fields that are both quantum-mechanically accurate and fast enough for long-timescale simulation. Recent large-scale pretrained machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approach density-functional-theory accuracy, but remain too slow to access the necessary timescales to converge transport properties. We provide a knowledge distillation procedure to transfer the accuracy of a large-scale "teacher" MLIP into fast, system-specific "students", without any additional ab initio data. Our distilled models run ~40x faster, reproduce teacher-predicted structural observables, and produce stable 20 ns trajectories in days, rather than the months the teacher would require. Across a diverse set of sodium- and lithium-ion electrolytes, student-predicted self-diffusivities, ionic conductivities, and shear viscosities track experiment and outperform classical force-field predictions, establishing distillation as a practical route to accurate, long-timescale simulations necessary for high-throughput electrolyte screening.

title: Transformer-inspired architectures make machine-learned electron densities accurate and transferable enough to bypass self-consistency
abstract: We introduce machine learning models that accurately predict the electron density, the central variable of density functional theory. They are built on Transformer-inspired architectures, which require little computation per parameter and can therefore be enlarged at low cost. The proposed models, SwinUNETR-V2 and its attention-free counterpart NeXtUNETR, achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on QM9, with normalized mean absolute errors in the density averaging 0.075% and 0.046%, respectively. The predicted densities are accurate enough to bypass the self-consistent iteration: a single Kohn-Sham step reproduces the self-consistent electronic structure. For NeXtUNETR, the median errors are 0.036 meV in the total energy, 0.65 meV/angstrom in the forces and 1.8 meV in the HOMO-LUMO gap. The forces not only recover the self-consistent minima in geometry optimization but also successfully drive ab initio molecular dynamics. Fine-tuned on small datasets, both networks also transfer accurately to systems containing elements absent from QM9 or larger than its molecules.

title: Differentiable Electronic Grand Canonical Learning for Electrochemistry
abstract: Electronic grand-canonical density functional theory captures how structure and electronic charge respond to electrode potential and, together with statistical mechanics, how these responses give rise to emergent phenomena. However, its computational cost limits the system sizes and sampling times accessible to first- principles simulations. Here, we introduce a differentiable architecture that represents the grand potential and obtains forces and electronic charge as its derivatives, exactly satisfying the mixed-derivative constraints required for thermodynamic consistency, and implement it within the equivariant MACE framework as GC- MACE. We demonstrate more accurate joint learning across multiple electrochemical interfaces and improved transferability to thicker water films relative to previous models, while enabling constant-potential simulations at substantially larger length and time scales than accessible to ab initio molecular dynamics. With broad training data, the framework offers a route to thermodynamically consistent foundation interatomic potentials for the electronic grand canonical ensemble

title: Photon Statistics and Light Squeezing Under Vibrational Strong Coupling from Real-Time Nuclear--Electronic Orbital Theory
abstract: Molecular polaritons have attracted great interest in recent years as a promising avenue for developing optical control of chemical processes. A major open question in this field is the role of quantum optical effects in understanding the molecular dynamics observed in cavities. In this work, we use our recently developed mean-field quantum and full-quantum real-time nuclear--electronic orbital time-dependent density functional theory methods to simulate photon statistics for a cavity mode strongly coupled to a molecular vibrational transition. Our comparative use of these two methods allows us to isolate the contributions of light--matter entanglement to the photon statistics. We consider three initial conditions of the cavity mode: a coherent state, a squeezed coherent state, and a single photon Fock state. These conditions span Poissonian, super-Poissonian, and sub-Poissonian photon statistics. Our full-quantum dynamics initialized with a coherent state show considerable super-Poissonian fluctuations of the photon statistics and light-squeezing of the cavity photons by the vibrational mode. These dynamics are particularly notable considering the quasi-classical properties of the coherent state. The squeezed coherent and Fock state initial conditions also demonstrate noteworthy fluctuations in the photon statistics. All three initial conditions reveal dynamics in the full-quantum photon statistics that differ considerably from the statistics obtained with the mean-field quantum method. Our results demonstrate the importance of considering quantum optical effects for molecules under strong coupling in certain situations.

title: Generalizing Density Functional Theory with a Particle-Hole Expansion
abstract: Strong electron correlation remains difficult to describe within conventional density functional approximations, particularly when natural-orbital occupations become strongly fractional. We introduce a systematic particle-hole expansion that generalizes density functional theory (DFT) through an explicit functional of the one-electron reduced density matrix. The previously derived cumulant-based correction emerges as the leading term and the thermal (entropic) correction as an infinite-order member whose coefficients are fixed by a single parameter. The expansion can be formulated as a moment problem solved by semidefinite programming with computational scaling comparable to DFT. We show that both the first- and second-order corrections yield closed-form natural-orbital occupations. Applications to periacenes and Fe-porphyrin demonstrate that the second-order correction substantially reduces excessive orbital fractionalization, yielding natural-orbital occupations and fundamental gaps in improved agreement with correlated calculations.
